items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Willie Humphrey said last night that George Field told him that Roy always was exact in playing trombone.

ctx.x: You think Roy Palmer played more trombone than you?

Well I think I'll give you an answer to that. I've been hearing Roy's records. I'll say this. Roy always could play better. Willie Humphrey said last night that George Field told him that Roy always was exact in playing trombone. No, I think Roy shaded me in musicianship for one thing, because Roy could read all the clefs. You see what I'm talking about? And I can. I'm just being truthful about it. But now I'm more aggressive than Roy was. It's a change of times. You see I had fellas tell me, I don't want you to…
Well he had a funny attack sometimes. But then other times he could play very clean. His brakes were extremely clean. Yeah, yeah.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I lived right across the street from Professor George Correa, and when I lived on Upper Line Street I was only two blocks from the Humphreys, and Mrs. Humphrey, old man Humphrey's daughter, taught me in the fourth grade at Tarly Farm School.

ctx.x: Piron. He played with Piron, the fellas, see, long before I thought about playing. But we went to school together in the third and fourth grade. Then there was Humphrey, Willie Humphrey, Willie Humphrey. The reason I'm breaking up some of these fellas, Bill, while reading the book that you gave me, I noted in there, I think it was Dominic who said that the musicians downtown read and
the musicians in downtown didn't read.
